reason: The current goal is to make supporting material, so I’ll start with the copied collagen instructions and protein machinery.
expectation: I expect the machinery to use the instructions as a step toward making collagen, though amino acids may also be needed.

alternatives.reason: Renewing surface cells seems relevant to rebuilding the skin, but the supporting material is the current goal.

effect: The copied instructions direct the repair cells’ protein machinery toward making collagen, connecting this work to the protein building seen in muscle cells.
reaction: The link between the same machinery and different tissue jobs is useful.
reason: Amino acids are the building blocks needed to make the collagen protein.
expectation: I expect the directed builders to join the amino acids into a collagen protein, perhaps needing further processing.

alternatives.reason: Surface renewal also matters for repair, but I want to continue making the supporting material first.

effect: The amino acids formed new collagen chains, and the result clarified that building them also uses energy.
reaction: The distinction between instructions and building material makes sense.
reason: The new chains likely need processing and export before they can support the damaged site.
expectation: I expect the membranes to process the collagen chains and move them out of the cells, though further assembly may be needed.

alternatives.reason: Surface renewal is relevant to repair, but I want to finish the supporting material first.

effect: The collagen material has been processed and exported, so it can now be assembled outside the cell.
reaction: Separating protein production from delivery makes the process clearer.
reason: Fiber-forming helpers seem like the next step toward making the supporting material.
expectation: I expect the exported precursors to be assembled into collagen fibers that can support the damaged site.

alternatives.reason: Surface renewal also matters, but I want to finish the supporting material first.

effect: The exported collagen material has formed supporting fibers outside the cells, ready to contribute to the damaged tissue.
reaction: It is satisfying to see the cell's work become a structure outside it.
reason: I'll add the new fibers to the body to support the damaged site.
expectation: I expect the fibers to help rebuild support at the scrape, though the surface may still need renewal.

alternatives.reason: Surface renewal also matters, but I want to use the fibers I just made first.

effect: The new fibers support the damaged region, and the next goal is to restore its surface coverage.
reaction: The distinction between sealing the scrape and rebuilding tissue is clear.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and it appears to start surface renewal.
expectation: I expect the signals to prompt the resident surface cells to renew or spread, though another step may be needed to cover the scrape.

effect: The local signals prompted surface cells to move and multiply, providing cells that can cover the repair.
reaction: The distinction between a signal and replacement material is useful.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and it should restore surface coverage.
expectation: I expect the spreading cells to cover the damaged area, though the tissue may still need further rebuilding.

effect: Surface coverage is restored while deeper repair continues, and the goal has shifted to lifting the glass.
reaction: The possibility of a scar makes the repair feel less like an instant reset.
reason: This is the only offered combination and addresses the new goal.
expectation: I expect the body to lift and hold the glass using its coordinated muscles and continuing supply of energy.

effect: The final result connects the repaired skin, muscle-cell energy use, nerve signals and blood supply to holding the glass still.
reaction: The idea that holding still requires continuing work is a satisfying conclusion.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making supporting fibers and adding them to the damaged site made the link between cell work and tissue structure concrete.

leastWorthwhile.text: The surface-renewal sequence was clear but offered only one combination at each step, so it felt less like a meaningful decision.

surprise.text: I was struck that restored surface coverage can coexist with deeper repair and a possible scar.

arbitrary.text: No action felt without a clear purpose, though the compatible-partner options guided the sequence and did not require discovering which parts fit.

continue.text: I would be somewhat interested in another chapter that connects cell work to an everyday action, although I would want more meaningful choices than the later steps offered.
